Look at your current to-dos. Find two tasks that take under two minutes — and finish them now.
Pick one task. Work on it for 25 minutes without switching, then take a real 5-minute break.
Put everything on your plate into four squares. Then pick one task from “Do now”.
Pick one thing you’ve been putting off. Count 5-4-3-2-1 out loud and take the first physical step at 1.
Complete one sentence: “After I [habit I already have], I will [tiny new habit].” Do it today.
Pick a topic you’re learning and explain it in simple words, as if to a curious 12-year-old. No notes.
Write down your goals. Keep the top three. Move the rest to a “Not now” list and leave it alone this week.
Block 50 minutes for one demanding task. Close everything else and silence your phone.
Take your most important task. List its steps and mark the one that moves it most. Start there.
Pick something you learned this week. Recall it from memory now, then check what you missed.
Pick one feed or app to skip today. Before opening anything, ask: do I need this right now?
Imagine your project failed completely six months from now. Write down why, then pick one step to reduce the biggest risk today.
Choose one skill or habit. Make it 1% better today with one small, specific change.
Answer three questions: what went well, what didn’t, and what you’ll change tomorrow.
